liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Never Trust A Woman** (2 reviews): Freshly heartbroken, the reviewer wanted to hear this one, known as Good Times Blues, and Brent started its opening riff; Reviewer's first time hearing Good Times Blues since Alpine in 1988 [23][27]
- **Stagger Lee** (1 review): Reviewer believes Jerry lost his voice here, explaining the run of songs before his next vocal tune [29]
- **Smokestack Lightning** (1 review): Closing the first set, it left the crowd dazed and smiling through the set break [21]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Huge video screens showed marching turtles during this song [29]

## Setlist highlights

- **5 Minute Long Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]
- **Nobody's Fault But Mine Jam**: back after 613 archived shows (3079 days) [32]

## The recordings

- **gd1990-07-23.147601.mtx.tobin.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 157 min [1]
- **gd1990-07-23.147602.dts.tobin.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 157 min [3]
- **gd1990-07-23.147778.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 160 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [5]
- **gd1990-07-23.147719.ultramatrix.sbd.miller.flac24**: soundboard; 19 songs; 160 min [7]
- **gd90-07-23.sbd.oconner.7612.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 149 min; rated 3.52/5 by 57 [13]. Said about its sound: Reviewer heard Brent more clearly than anyone else that night; Inside the building a built-in balcony acted as a baffle, so sound bounced around and was poor; Reviewer's video of the show looks better than the tape sounds [24][25][26][27]

## Around the show

- Reviewer found a large crystal on the ground just inside the fence and kept it in his car for years [21]
- Reviewer saw it as the end of an era, marking Brent's final performance [22]
- Reviewer attended the tour's last show from 15th row center, his best seats ever at a Dead show [23]
- Reviewer's first show; lost a friend in the parking lot, met new people, and found the crowd lovely [24]
- The lawn sounded better but was so overcrowded that people could barely breathe or move [25]
- Lawn was far too crowded, traffic was bad, and reviewer bought a ticket in standstill traffic on I-80 [26]
- Reviewer disliked the venue and considered it Brent's last show, and not a great one [27]
- Reviewer says Brent looked at Jerry while singing his final solo lines, in the encore [29]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1990-07-23.147601.mtx.tobin.flac16**: transferred by SBD + AUD Matrix 2 Source Mix (44/16) by Kevin Tobin; source: SBD + AUD Matrix 2 Source Mix (44/16) [1]. Also: Matrix mix made by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in September 2019 by Trader Little Helper [1]
- **gd1990-07-23.147602.dts.tobin.flac16**: transferred by DTS-Audio-CD 5.1 Mix by Kevin Tobin; source: DTS-Audio-CD 5.1 Mix [3]. Also: Matrix mix by an archive.org user, packaged as a DTS surround audio CD format, converted to FLAC in 2019 [3]
- **gd1990-07-23.147778.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-X90) [5]. Also: Ultramatrix soundboard source in 16-bit 44.1 kHz; two different sets of masters were combined to complete the show [5]
- **gd1990-07-23.147719.ultramatrix.sbd.miller.flac24**: taped by Don Pearson; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-X90) [7]. Also: Ultramatrix soundboard transfers and mastering by Charlie Miller, 24-bit, combining two different sets of masters to complete the show [7]
- **gd90-07-23.sbd.oconner.7612.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [13]
